The server may generate them, but any\\n167\\tclient-provided ID must be validated before use.\\n168\\t\\n169\\t## Session Manifest\\n170\\t\\n171\\tEach established session JSONL file must have a companion manifest at the same path stem. The manifest must not be written for a brand-new chat until after the first assistant message has completed and the short chat description has been generated or has fallen back deterministically:\\n172\\t\\n173\\t```json\\n174\\t{\\n175\\t  \\\"schemaVersion\\\": 1,\\n176\\t  \\\"pile\\\": \\\"default\\\",\\n177\\t  \\\"sessionId\\\": \\\"01J...\\\",\\n178\\t  \\\"chatName\\\": \\\"Fix login redirect\\\",\\n179\\t  \\\"description\\\": \\\"Short generated description\\\",\\n180\\t  \\\"rootDirectory\\\": \\\"projects/example-app\\\",\\n181\\t  \\\"createdAt\\\": \\\"2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z\\\",\\n182\\t  \\\"updatedAt\\\": \\\"2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z\\\",\\n183\\t  \\\"lastOpenedAt\\\": \\\"2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z\\\",\\n184\\t  \\\"model\\\": {\\n185\\t    \\\"provider\\\": \\\"openai\\\",\\n186\\t    \\\"id\\\": \\\"gpt-5-codex\\\"\\n187\\t  },\\n188\\t  \\\"pi\\\": {\\n189\\t    \\\"sessionFile\\\": \\\"data/sheaf-chat/sessions/piles/default/01J....jsonl\\\",\\n190\\t    \\\"extensionVersion\\\": \\\"...\\\"\\n191\\t  },\\n192\\t  \\\"history\\\": {\\n193\\t    \\\"messageCount\\\": 0,\\n194\\t    \\\"lastSequence\\\": 0\\n195\\t  }\\n196\\t}\\n197\\t```\\n198\\t\\n199\\t`rootDirectory` should be stored as an absolute path when possible. On resume,\\n200\\tthe manifest root is authoritative for constructing the scoped tools.\\n201\\t\\n202\\tWhen a new session receives its first user message, send that message to a side\\n203\\tagent or summarization path to generate a short chat name/description. Do not\\n204\\tsave the manifest yet. Wait until the first assistant message has completed,\\n205\\tthen write the initial manifest containing the root directory, model, generated\\n206\\tchat name/description, and session metadata. If summarization fails, use a\\n207\\tdeterministic fallback such as the first line of the user message, truncated.\\n208\\tThis avoids persisting manifests for abandoned blank sessions or chats that never\\n209\\tproduce an assistant response.\\n210\\t\\n211\\t## Agent Lifecycle\\n212\\t\\n213\\tThe backend keeps an in-memory registry keyed by `(pile, sessionId)`.\\n214\\t\\n215\\tStates:\\n216\\t\\n217\\t- `cold`: manifest/session file exists on disk, no Pi agent is running.\\n218\\t- `starting`: an agent is being created or resumed.\\n219\\t- `active`: an agent is running and may have zero or more WebSocket clients.\\n220\\t- `idle`: an active agent has no recent client or model activity and is eligible\\n221\\t  for offload.\\n222\\t- `stopping`: session state is being flushed and the agent is being released.\\n223\\t- `failed`: startup/resume failed; clients receive an error event.\\n224\\t\\n225\\tBehavior:\\n226\\t\\n227\\t- New chat: validate pile and root directory, allocate a session ID and JSONL\\n228\\t  session path, create a Pi agent with repository-provided config and scoped\\n229\\t  tools, then accept the first user message. Do not write the manifest until\\n230\\t  after the first assistant message completes.\\n231\\t- Resume hot chat: if `(pile, sessionId)` is already active, attach the WebSocket\\n232\\t  to that agent and replay enough recent history for the client.\\n233\\t- Resume cold chat: load manifest, validate the session JSONL exists, recreate\\n234\\t  the scoped tool environment from the manifest, resume the Pi session file, and\\n235\\t  attach the WebSocket.\\n236\\t- Offload: after `agent_idle_offload_seconds` with no connected clients and no\\n237\\t  active run, flush session state to disk and release the agent. Never offload in\\n238\\t  the middle of a tool call or agent turn.\\n239\\t- Reconnect: a client may reconnect to the same session and ask for events after\\n240\\t  its last acknowledged sequence.\\n241\\t\\n242\\t## Scoped Tool Requirements\\n243\\t\\n244\\tThe Sheaf Chat Pi extension must provide scoped file and search tools for the\\n245\\tsession `rootDirectory`. It must not expose Bash, shell execution, or any general\\n246\\tcommand-execution tool.\\n247\\t\\n248\\tRequired tools:\\n249\\t\\n250\\t- `read`: same input/output shape and argument names as Pi's built-in `read`\\n251\\t  tool, but restricted to UTF-8 text files under the root and returning\\n252\\t  line-numbered excerpts with paths relativized to the root.\\n253\\t- `write`: same input/output shape and argument names as Pi's built-in `write`\\n254\\t  tool, but restricted to creating or overwriting files under the root and\\n255\\t  reporting only root-relative paths.\\n256\\t- `edit`: same input/output shape and argument names as Pi's built-in `edit`\\n257\\t  tool, including exact text replacement semantics, but restricted to files under\\n258\\t  the root and reporting only root-relative paths.\\n259\\t- `list`: list directory entries under the root with file type, size, and\\n260\\t  modified time.\\n261\\t- `tree`: return a bounded directory tree with ignore rules for dependency,\\n262\\t  build, VCS, cache, and large generated directories.\\n263\\t- `find_files`: ripgrep/fd-like file discovery by glob, extension, path segment,\\n264\\t  include/exclude globs, max depth, and limit.\\n265\\t- `search_text`: ripgrep-like full-text search with literal or regex modes,\\n266\\t  case sensitivity, include/exclude globs, context lines, multiline-safe output,\\n267\\t  binary-file skipping, and match limits.\\n268\\t- `file_info`: stat a relative path and report canonical in-root metadata.\\n269\\t\\n270\\tTool rules:\\n271\\t\\n272\\t- `read`, `write`, and `edit` must preserve Pi's normal tool schema so existing\\n273\\t  Pi prompting and model behavior remain compatible. Only path interpretation,\\n274\\t  validation, and result path rendering change.\\n275\\t- Tool path arguments use paths relative to the root directory.\\n276\\t- Absolute path input is rejected unless converted to a path under the root and\\n277\\t  returned/displayed as relative.\\n278\\t- Normalize, resolve symlinks where relevant, and verify the final target remains\\n279\\t  inside the canonical root before every filesystem operation.\\n280\\t- Search tools must provide enough capability to replace normal shell `rg`,\\n281\\t  `find`, `ls`, and lightweight code-navigation usage without granting arbitrary\\n282\\t  process execution.\\n283\\t- Tool results must redact or relativize absolute host paths under the root.\\n284\\t- Tool results must not reveal parent directories or files outside the root.\\n285\\t- Attempts to escape the root should emit a visible AGUI activity/control event\\n286\\t  and be logged for audit.\\n287\\t\\n288\\t## Providers And Models\\n289\\t\\n290\\tInitial providers:\\n291\\t\\n292\\t1. OpenAI subscription/OAuth, with OAuth data stored under `data/sheaf-chat/`.\\n293\\t2. Local inference, using `sheaf_chat.local_inference_url` from config and\\n294\\t   `sheaf_chat.local_api_key` from `config/api_keys.json`.\\n295\\t\\n296\\tThe model list exposed to browsers must merge:\\n297\\t\\n298\\t- GPT/OpenAI models available through the configured OpenAI subscription; and\\n299\\t- models reported by or configured for the local inference endpoint.\\n300\\t\\n301\\tThe server should expose model metadata indicating provider, model ID, display\\n302\\tname, context capability if known, and whether the model is currently available.\\n303\\t\\n304\\t## REST API\\n305\\t\\n306\\tAll JSON responses should include stable machine-readable errors:\\n307\\t\\n308\\t```json\\n309\\t{ \\\"error\\\": { \\\"code\\\": \\\"not_found\\\", \\\"message\\\": \\\"...\\\" } }\\n310\\t```\\n311\\t\\n312\\tRequired endpoints:\\n313\\t\\n314\\t- `GET /api/health` — service health and version.\\n315\\t- `GET /api/piles` — list piles with session counts and latest update time.\\n316\\t- `POST /api/piles` — create a pile. Body: `{ \\\"pile\\\": \\\"name\\\" }`.\\n317\\t- `GET /api/piles/:pile/sessions` — list session manifests in a pile, newest\\n318\\t  first, excluding heavy message history.\\n319\\t- `GET /api/piles/:pile/sessions/:sessionId` — return one manifest.\\n320\\t- `POST /api/piles/:pile/sessions` — create a new blank session shell. Body\\n321\\t  includes `{ \\\"rootDirectory\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"model\\\": { \\\"provider\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"...\\\" } }`.\\n322\\t  Response includes `sessionId`, provisional session metadata, and WebSocket URL,\\n323\\t  but not a persisted manifest. The manifest is written only after the first\\n324\\t  assistant message completes. The first user message may be sent over the\\n325\\t  WebSocket rather than this REST call.\\n326\\t- `GET /api/piles/:pile/sessions/:sessionId/history?before=<cursor>&limit=<n>` —\\n327\\t  optional REST fallback for paged history if WebSocket history is not available.\\n328\\t- `GET /api/models` — list available models.\\n329\\t\\n330\\tThe browser should normally use WebSocket history requests, but the REST history\\n331\\tfallback is useful for testing and recovery.\\n332\\t\\n333\\t## WebSocket Protocol\\n334\\t\\n335\\t### URL And Connection\\n336\\t\\n337\\tUse one WebSocket route for both new and resumed sessions:\\n338\\t\\n339\\t```text\\n340\\t/ws/chat?p=<pile>&session=<sessionId>&client=<clientId>&after=<sequence>\\n341\\t```\\n342\\t\\n343\\tFor a newly-created blank session, the client first calls\\n344\\t`POST /api/piles/:pile/sessions`, then opens this WebSocket and sends the first\\n345\\t`client.user_message`.\\n346\\t\\n347\\tQuery parameters:\\n348\\t\\n349\\t- `p` / `pile` (required): pile name.\\n350\\t- `session` (required): session ID.\\n351\\t- `client` (optional): stable browser client ID for reconnect diagnostics.\\n352\\t- `after` (optional): last server sequence the client has processed. If present,\\n353\\t  server sends all available envelopes after that sequence before live mode.\\n354\\t\\n355\\tAll WebSocket frames are UTF-8 JSON objects. Binary frames are not required for\\n356\\tquest zero.\\n357\\t\\n358\\t### Envelope\\n359\\t\\n360\\tEvery server-to-client and client-to-server frame uses this envelope:\\n361\\t\\n362\\t```ts\\n363\\ttype ChatEnvelope = {\\n364\\t  v: 1;\\n365\\t  kind: string;\\n366\\t  id: string;              // unique frame id generated by sender\\n367\\t  pile: string;\\n368\\t  sessionId: string;\\n369\\t  clientId?: string;\\n370\\t  sequence?: number;       // server-assigned monotonically increasing sequence\\n371\\t  timestamp: string;       // ISO-8601\\n372\\t  payload?: unknown;\\n373\\t};\\n374\\t```\\n375\\t\\n376\\tServer-assigned `sequence` values are strictly increasing per session and are the\\n377\\tbasis for replay, acknowledgements, and lazy loading. Client frames do not set\\n378\\t`sequence`.\\n379\\t\\n380\\t### Server-To-Client Kinds\\n381\\t\\n382\\t#### `server.hello`\\n383\\t\\n384\\tFirst frame after a successful connection.\\n385\\t\\n386\\t```json\\n387\\t{\\n388\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"server.hello\\\",\\n389\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n390\\t    \\\"connectionId\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n391\\t    \\\"manifest\\\": null,\\n392\\t    \\\"provisionalSession\\\": {\\n393\\t      \\\"rootDirectory\\\": \\\"projects/example-app\\\",\\n394\\t      \\\"model\\\": { \\\"provider\\\": \\\"openai\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"gpt-5-codex\\\" }\\n395\\t    },\\n396\\t    \\\"latestSequence\\\": 123,\\n397\\t    \\\"historyWindow\\\": { \\\"oldestSequence\\\": 80, \\\"newestSequence\\\": 123 },\\n398\\t    \\\"models\\\": [],\\n399\\t    \\\"activeModel\\\": { \\\"provider\\\": \\\"openai\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"gpt-5-codex\\\" }\\n400\\t  }\\n401\\t}\\n402\\t```\\n403\\t\\n404\\t#### `history.page`\\n405\\t\\n406\\tA page of historical AGUI events or snapshot messages. Sent in response to\\n407\\t`client.history_request` and optionally during connection bootstrap.\\n408\\t\\n409\\t```json\\n410\\t{\\n411\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"history.page\\\",\\n412\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n413\\t    \\\"requestId\\\": \\\"client-frame-id\\\",\\n414\\t    \\\"direction\\\": \\\"before\\\",\\n415\\t    \\\"events\\\": [ { \\\"type\\\": \\\"TEXT_MESSAGE_START\\\" } ],\\n416\\t    \\\"messages\\\": [ { \\\"id\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"...\\\" } ],\\n417\\t    \\\"oldestSequence\\\": 1,\\n418\\t    \\\"newestSequence\\\": 50,\\n419\\t    \\\"hasMoreBefore\\\": false,\\n420\\t    \\\"hasMoreAfter\\\": true\\n421\\t  }\\n422\\t}\\n423\\t```\\n424\\t\\n425\\tThe server may send either AGUI events or AGUI-compatible message snapshots. If\\n426\\tsnapshots are sent, they must match message shapes accepted by\\n427\\t`projects/web/src/agui-chat.js`.\\n428\\t\\n429\\t#### `agui.event`\\n430\\t\\n431\\tOne AGUI event mapped from Pi output or generated by Sheaf Chat.\\n432\\t\\n433\\t```json\\n434\\t{\\n435\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"agui.event\\\",\\n436\\t  \\\"sequence\\\": 124,\\n437\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n438\\t    \\\"type\\\": \\\"TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT\\\",\\n439\\t    \\\"messageId\\\": \\\"assistant-1\\\",\\n440\\t    \\\"delta\\\": \\\"Hello\\\"\\n441\\t  }\\n442\\t}\\n443\\t```\\n444\\t\\n445\\t`payload` must validate against `structure/schemas/ag_ui_events.schema.json` when\\n446\\tpossible. Preserve raw Pi events in `rawEvent` for debugging unless they contain\\n447\\tsecrets or host-only paths.\\n448\\t\\n449\\t#### `chat.user_message`\\n450\\t\\n451\\tBroadcast copy of an accepted user message. The originating client receives this\\n452\\ttoo, so all clients render identical user turns.\\n453\\t\\n454\\t```json\\n455\\t{\\n456\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"chat.user_message\\\",\\n457\\t  \\\"sequence\\\": 125,\\n458\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n459\\t    \\\"messageId\\\": \\\"user-...\\\",\\n460\\t    \\\"text\\\": \\\"Please inspect src/app.ts\\\",\\n461\\t    \\\"attachments\\\": [],\\n462\\t    \\\"steer\\\": true\\n463\\t  }\\n464\\t}\\n465\\t```\\n466\\t\\n467\\tThe server should also emit equivalent AGUI text message events so generic AGUI\\n468\\treducers can display the message.\\n469\\t\\n470\\t#### `session.updated`\\n471\\t\\n472\\tManifest or session metadata changed, such as initial manifest creation after the\\n473\\tfirst assistant message, generated chat name, root display, message count, or\\n474\\tactive model.\\n475\\t\\n476\\t#### `model.changed`\\n477\\t\\n478\\tThe active model changed for future turns or, if Pi supports it, for the current\\n479\\trun.\\n480\\t\\n481\\t#### `agent.status`\\n482\\t\\n483\\tLifecycle/status update. Payload examples: `{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"starting\\\" }`,\\n484\\t`{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"active\\\" }`, `{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"offloading\\\" }`,\\n485\\t`{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"resumed\\\" }`.\\n486\\t\\n487\\t#### `server.caught_up`\\n488\\t\\n489\\tThe server has finished replaying requested backlog and subsequent frames are\\n490\\tlive. This mirrors the existing Quest Runner dashboard behavior.\\n491\\t\\n492\\t#### `server.error`\\n493\\t\\n494\\tRecoverable or fatal error.\\n495\\t\\n496\\t```json\\n497\\t{\\n498\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"server.error\\\",\\n499\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n500\\t    \\\"code\\\": \\\"root_escape_denied\\\",\\n501\\t    \\\"message\\\": \\\"Path is outside the session root\\\",\\n502\\t    \\\"fatal\\\": false,\\n503\\t    \\\"requestId\\\": \\\"...\\\"\\n504\\t  }\\n505\\t}\\n506\\t```\\n507\\t\\n508\\t#### `server.pong`\\n509\\t\\n510\\tResponse to `client.ping`.\\n511\\t\\n512\\t### Client-To-Server Kinds\\n513\\t\\n514\\t#### `client.hello`\\n515\\t\\n516\\tOptional client capabilities after socket open.\\n517\\t\\n518\\t```json\\n519\\t{\\n520\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.hello\\\",\\n521\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n522\\t    \\\"supportsSnapshots\\\": true,\\n523\\t    \\\"supportsLazyHistory\\\": true,\\n524\\t    \\\"lastSeenSequence\\\": 123\\n525\\t  }\\n526\\t}\\n527\\t```\\n528\\t\\n529\\t#### `client.user_message`\\n530\\t\\n531\\tSubmit a user message.\\n532\\t\\n533\\t```json\\n534\\t{\\n535\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.user_message\\\",\\n536\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n537\\t    \\\"messageId\\\": \\\"client-generated-id\\\",\\n538\\t    \\\"text\\\": \\\"Continue, but use the local model.\\\",\\n539\\t    \\\"attachments\\\": [],\\n540\\t    \\\"steer\\\": true\\n541\\t  }\\n542\\t}\\n543\\t```\\n544\\t\\n545\\tRules:\\n546\\t\\n547\\t- The server validates, persists, sequences, and broadcasts the message before or\\n548\\t  while delivering it to the agent.\\n549\\t- If an agent turn is already running, the new message must steer the ongoing\\n550\\t  conversation if Pi supports steering/queueing. If Pi cannot steer mid-turn, the\\n551\\t  message must be queued as the next user input and all clients must still see it\\n552\\t  immediately.\\n553\\t- The server must de-duplicate by `messageId` for reconnect/retry safety.\\n554\\t\\n555\\t#### `client.history_request`\\n556\\t\\n557\\tRequest older or newer events/messages.\\n558\\t\\n559\\t```json\\n560\\t{\\n561\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.history_request\\\",\\n562\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n563\\t    \\\"before\\\": 80,\\n564\\t    \\\"after\\\": null,\\n565\\t    \\\"limit\\\": 50,\\n566\\t    \\\"prefer\\\": \\\"snapshots\\\"\\n567\\t  }\\n568\\t}\\n569\\t```\\n570\\t\\n571\\tSupported modes:\\n572\\t\\n573\\t- `{ \\\"before\\\": sequence }`: page older history for scroll-up loading.\\n574\\t- `{ \\\"after\\\": sequence }`: replay missed events after reconnect.\\n575\\t- no cursor: return latest page large enough to populate the screen.\\n576\\t\\n577\\tThe server responds with `history.page` and must not block live `agui.event`\\n578\\tbroadcasts while reading history.\\n579\\t\\n580\\t#### `client.model_select`\\n581\\t\\n582\\tSwitch model.\\n583\\t\\n584\\t```json\\n585\\t{\\n586\\t  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.model_select\\\",\\n587\\t  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n588\\t    \\\"provider\\\": \\\"local\\\",\\n589\\t    \\\"id\\\": \\\"qwen3-coder\\\",\\n590\\t    \\\"applyTo\\\": \\\"next_turn\\\"\\n591\\t  }\\n592\\t}\\n593\\t```\\n594\\t\\n595\\tIf AGUI later standardizes model selection, this control message may be mapped to\\n596\\tthat standard, but the Sheaf Chat protocol must support it now. The server\\n597\\tvalidates availability, updates the manifest, broadcasts `model.changed`, and\\n598\\tapplies the change to Pi according to SDK capabilities.\\n599\\t\\n600\\t#### `client.ack`\\n601\\t\\n602\\tAcknowledge processed server sequence.\\n603\\t\\n604\\t```json\\n605\\t{ \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.ack\\\", \\\"payload\\\": { \\\"sequence\\\": 125 } }\\n606\\t```\\n607\\t\\n608\\tAcks are used for diagnostics and reconnect hints. They are not required for\\n609\\texactly-once delivery.\\n610\\t\\n611\\t#### `client.cancel` / `client.stop_generating`\\n612\\t\\n613\\tRequest cancellation of the current agent turn if supported. The server\\n614\\tbroadcasts status and emits AGUI lifecycle close/error events as needed.\\n615\\t\\n616\\t#### `client.ping`\\n617\\t\\n618\\tKeepalive. Server responds with `server.pong`.\\n619\\t\\n620\\t### Ordering And Synchronization\\n621\\t\\n622\\t- The server assigns sequence numbers after accepting an event for a session.\\n623\\t- All attached clients receive frames in sequence order for that session.\\n624\\t- User messages are persisted and broadcast even if the agent later fails.\\n625\\t- Agent output events are broadcast to all current clients and appended to the\\n626\\t  session log/history index.\\n627\\t- On reconnect, the client supplies `after=<lastSequence>` or sends\\n628\\t  `client.history_request` with `after`. The server replays missed frames, sends\\n629\\t  `server.caught_up`, then continues live.\\n630\\t- When multiple clients send user messages concurrently, the server serializes\\n631\\t  them by acceptance time and sequence number. That sequence is the conversation\\n632\\t  order.\\n633\\t\\n634\\t### AGUI Mapping Requirements\\n635\\t\\n636\\tThe server may either:\\n637\\t\\n638\\t1. reuse the existing Python mapping logic through a subprocess/module boundary;\\n639\\t   or\\n640\\t2. implement an equivalent TypeScript mapper for Pi JSON events.\\n641\\t\\n642\\tA TypeScript mapper is preferred for a Node-only backend if it can be tested\\n643\\tagainst the existing AGUI schema. Required mapped surfaces include:\\n644\\t\\n645\\t- user text messages;\\n646\\t- assistant text stream start/content/end;\\n647\\t- reasoning/thinking deltas where Pi exposes them;\\n648\\t- tool call start/arguments/result/end;\\n649\\t- run/turn start, finish, cancellation, and errors;\\n650\\t- custom Sheaf Chat activity events for path enforcement, model changes, and\\n651\\t  lifecycle status.\\n652\\t\\n653\\tUnrecognized Pi events must not be dropped. Emit an AGUI `RAW` or custom\\n654\\tactivity event with sanitized payload and add tests so known Pi event forms map\\n655\\tcleanly over time.\\n656\\t\\n657\\t## Browser UI Requirements\\n658\\t\\n659\\tExtend the existing shared AGUI chat assets without breaking their current\\n660\\tread-only uses.\\n661\\t\\n662\\tThe browser UI has three primary screens with straightforward navigation:\\n663\\t\\n664\\t1. Piles screen: the top-level screen lists piles and includes controls to create\\n665\\t   a pile.\\n666\\t2. Sessions screen: selecting a pile shows sessions in that pile and includes\\n667\\t   controls to start a new session in that pile.\\n668\\t3. Chat screen: selecting a session opens the chat for that `(pile, sessionId)`.\\n669\\t\\n670\\tEach screen must provide a clear way to go back to the previous screen. The chat\\n671\\tscreen goes back to the sessions list for its pile; the sessions screen goes back\\n672\\tto the piles list. Browser history/back-button behavior should match this screen\\n673\\tnavigation where practical.\\n674\\t\\n675\\tRequired capabilities:\\n676\\t\\n677\\t- render the piles screen from `GET /api/piles`;\\n678\\t- render the sessions screen from `GET /api/piles/:pile/sessions`;\\n679\\t- render AGUI event streams and message snapshots on the chat screen;\\n680\\t- open a WebSocket for a selected `(pile, sessionId)`;\\n681\\t- show connection/agent/model status;\\n682\\t- on desktop, send text messages with Enter and support multiline input with\\n683\\t  Shift+Enter;\\n684\\t- on mobile/touch layouts, Enter should insert a newline and sending should use\\n685\\t  an explicit in-app Send button rather than relying on the keyboard Enter key;\\n686\\t- disable or visibly queue sends while disconnected;\\n687\\t- render user messages from server broadcasts rather than relying only on local\\n688\\t  echo;\\n689\\t- lazy-load older history when the user scrolls near the top;\\n690\\t- preserve scroll position when prepending older history;\\n691\\t- request a latest history page on initial load large enough to fill the viewport;\\n692\\t- reconnect with last seen sequence and request missed events;\\n693\\t- expose model selection and send `client.model_select`;\\n694\\t- handle multiple connected clients without duplicate local rendering;\\n695\\t- render tool calls and reasoning in compact expandable blocks;\\n696\\t- work well on mobile screens.\\n697\\t\\n698\\tMobile requirements:\\n699\\t\\n700\\t- responsive single-column layout;\\n701\\t- composer fixed or sticky at the bottom without hiding the last message;\\n702\\t- touch-friendly controls with at least 44px hit targets;\\n703\\t- textarea grows to a reasonable maximum height;\\n704\\t- avoid horizontal overflow for code, tool args, and long paths;\\n705\\t- tolerate virtual keyboard viewport changes;\\n706\\t- keep pile/session navigation usable on narrow {\"file\": {\"content\": \"# Sheaf Chat\\n\\n## Quest Overview\\n\\nBuild Sheaf Chat as a Sheaf service for browser-based conversations with Pi agents.\\nThe project owns:\\n\\n- a Node.js backend under `projects/sheaf-chat/` that manages embedded Pi agent\\n  sessions;\\n- a Pi extension and repository-local Pi configuration used by those agents;\\n- a browser chat UI, extending the existing AGUI chat assets in `projects/web/`;\\n- session storage, manifests, pile management, provider/model selection, and a\\n  WebSocket protocol suitable for robust multi-client chat.\\n\\nThe service must be registered as `sheaf-chat` on port `9004` in\\n`config/services.json`.\\n\\n## Reference Documentation\\n\\nImplementers that are not Pi agents should still use the installed Pi\\nintegration documentation as the authoritative source for Pi embedding,\\nextensions, sessions, configuration, and tool APIs:\\n\\n- Pi README: `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md`\\n- Pi extension docs: `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/extensions.md`\\n- Pi SDK docs: `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/sdk.md`\\n- Pi custom providers/models docs:\\n  `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/custom-provider.md`\\n  and `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/models.md`\\n\\nAGUI-related in-repo references:\\n\\n- AGUI schema: `structure/schemas/ag_ui_events.schema.json`\\n- Existing AGUI reducer/UI: `projects/web/src/agui-chat.js` and\\n  `projects/web/src/agui-chat.css`\\n- Existing Python mapper: `projects/quest-runner/src/quest_runner_service/agui_mapper.py`\\n- Mapping notes: `projects/quest-runner/docs/reference/agui-mapping.md`\\n\\n## Goals\\n\\n- Create a Node backend that lazily creates, resumes, multiplexes, and offloads\\n  Pi agents.\\n- Persist Pi session JSONL files and companion manifests under Sheaf Chat data.\\n- Organize sessions into named piles and require `(pile, sessionId)` for all\\n  session references.\\n- Provide REST APIs for pile/session/model discovery and WebSocket URLs for live\\n  chat.\\n- Provide a bidirectional WebSocket protocol that carries AGUI events plus Sheaf\\n  Chat control messages.\\n- Support multiple browser WebSockets connected to the same underlying agent.\\n- Propagate every user message and live agent event to all clients attached to\\n  that session.\\n- Support lazy loading of older messages while keeping the browser synchronized\\n  with live events.\\n- Enforce a per-session root directory at the tools layer. The agent must not be\\n  able to read, write, list, execute against, or reference paths outside that\\n  root or its descendants.\\n- Make agents independent of machine/global Pi configuration. The service must\\n  provide all Pi config, extensions, provider configuration, and tool surfaces\\n  needed for each session.\\n- Support OpenAI subscription/OAuth and a local inference endpoint.\\n- Extend the existing shared AGUI chat UI for send-message, lazy history loading,\\n  model switching, reconnect handling, and mobile use.\\n\\n## Non-Goals\\n\\n- Do not depend on a developer's global `~/.pi` configuration for runtime\\n  behavior.\\n- Do not allow tools to escape the session root through absolute paths, `..`,\\n  symlinks, shell working-directory tricks, environment variables, or generated\\n  absolute path references.\\n- Do not require all historical messages to load before a conversation can be\\n  displayed.\\n- Do not create a second service registry outside `config/services.json`.\\n- Do not commit real API keys or OAuth tokens.\\n- Do not move project-specific Sheaf Chat UI logic into `projects/web/` unless it\\n  is genuinely reusable by other services.\\n\\n## Project Layout\\n\\nRequired top-level project layout:\\n\\n```text\\nprojects/sheaf-chat/\\n  README.md\\n  Makefile\\n  docs/\\n  quests/\\n  src/\\n  tests/\\n```\\n\\nRecommended implementation layout:\\n\\n```text\\nprojects/sheaf-chat/src/\\n  server/              # HTTP/WebSocket server and REST APIs\\n  agents/              # Pi SDK adapter, agent lifecycle, offload/resume logic\\n  extensions/          # Sheaf Chat Pi extension and root-scoped tools\\n  storage/             # piles, session manifests, JSONL/history readers\\n  agui/                # Pi-to-AGUI mapper if implemented in TypeScript\\n  ui/                  # service-owned browser page and JS\\n```\\n\\nShared, generic AGUI rendering improvements may be made in `projects/web/src/`.\\nSheaf Chat-specific browser code should remain under `projects/sheaf-chat/src/ui/`.\\n\\n## Service Registration And Configuration\\n\\nRegister the service in `config/services.json`:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"name\\\": \\\"sheaf-chat\\\",\\n  \\\"host\\\": \\\"0.0.0.0\\\",\\n  \\\"port\\\": 9004,\\n  \\\"home_path\\\": \\\"/\\\",\\n  \\\"command\\\": \\\"make sheaf-chat-run\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThere is project configuration to `config/global_config.json` or another existing\\nrepo-level non-secret config file if that file already owns service-wide knobs.\\nAt minimum Sheaf Chat needs:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n    \\\"local_inference_url\\\": \\\".../v1\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThere is a secrets in `config/api_keys.json`, with an example in\\n`config/api_keys.example.json`:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"local_inference_api_key\\\": \\\"...\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nOpenAI OAuth data for Sheaf Chat must be stored under the project's data\\ndirectory and must not be read from global Pi configuration. The API key file may\\ncontain bootstrap secrets or references, but persisted OAuth material belongs in\\n`data/sheaf-chat/auth/openai/` or an equivalent documented subdirectory.\\n\\n## Data Layout\\n\\nRuntime data belongs under `data/sheaf-chat/`:\\n\\n```text\\ndata/sheaf-chat/\\n  auth/\\n    openai/                 # OpenAI OAuth/subscription material\\n  sessions/\\n    piles/\\n      <pile>/\\n        <sessionId>.jsonl   # Pi session/event log\\n        <sessionId>.manifest.json\\n```\\n\\nA pile is exactly one subdirectory under `data/sheaf-chat/sessions/piles/`.\\nPile names must be validated as safe relative path segments. Recommended rule:\\n`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` and reject `.`, `..`, slashes, backslashes,\\nempty names, and names that normalize differently.\\n\\nSession IDs must also be safe file stems. The server may generate them, but any\\nclient-provided ID must be validated before use.\\n\\n## Session Manifest\\n\\nEach established session JSONL file must have a companion manifest at the same path stem. The manifest must not be written for a brand-new chat until after the first assistant message has completed and the short chat description has been generated or has fallen back deterministically:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"schemaVersion\\\": 1,\\n  \\\"pile\\\": \\\"default\\\",\\n  \\\"sessionId\\\": \\\"01J...\\\",\\n  \\\"chatName\\\": \\\"Fix login redirect\\\",\\n  \\\"description\\\": \\\"Short generated description\\\",\\n  \\\"rootDirectory\\\": \\\"projects/example-app\\\",\\n  \\\"createdAt\\\": \\\"2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z\\\",\\n  \\\"updatedAt\\\": \\\"2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z\\\",\\n  \\\"lastOpenedAt\\\": \\\"2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z\\\",\\n  \\\"model\\\": {\\n    \\\"provider\\\": \\\"openai\\\",\\n    \\\"id\\\": \\\"gpt-5-codex\\\"\\n  },\\n  \\\"pi\\\": {\\n    \\\"sessionFile\\\": \\\"data/sheaf-chat/sessions/piles/default/01J....jsonl\\\",\\n    \\\"extensionVersion\\\": \\\"...\\\"\\n  },\\n  \\\"history\\\": {\\n    \\\"messageCount\\\": 0,\\n    \\\"lastSequence\\\": 0\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n`rootDirectory` should be stored as an absolute path when possible. On resume,\\nthe manifest root is authoritative for constructing the scoped tools.\\n\\nWhen a new session receives its first user message, send that message to a side\\nagent or summarization path to generate a short chat name/description. Do not\\nsave the manifest yet. Wait until the first assistant message has completed,\\nthen write the initial manifest containing the root directory, model, generated\\nchat name/description, and session metadata. If summarization fails, use a\\ndeterministic fallback such as the first line of the user message, truncated.\\nThis avoids persisting manifests for abandoned blank sessions or chats that never\\nproduce an assistant response.\\n\\n## Agent Lifecycle\\n\\nThe backend keeps an in-memory registry keyed by `(pile, sessionId)`.\\n\\nStates:\\n\\n- `cold`: manifest/session file exists on disk, no Pi agent is running.\\n- `starting`: an agent is being created or resumed.\\n- `active`: an agent is running and may have zero or more WebSocket clients.\\n- `idle`: an active agent has no recent client or model activity and is eligible\\n  for offload.\\n- `stopping`: session state is being flushed and the agent is being released.\\n- `failed`: startup/resume failed; clients receive an error event.\\n\\nBehavior:\\n\\n- New chat: validate pile and root directory, allocate a session ID and JSONL\\n  session path, create a Pi agent with repository-provided config and scoped\\n  tools, then accept the first user message. Do not write the manifest until\\n  after the first assistant message completes.\\n- Resume hot chat: if `(pile, sessionId)` is already active, attach the WebSocket\\n  to that agent and replay enough recent history for the client.\\n- Resume cold chat: load manifest, validate the session JSONL exists, recreate\\n  the scoped tool environment from the manifest, resume the Pi session file, and\\n  attach the WebSocket.\\n- Offload: after `agent_idle_offload_seconds` with no connected clients and no\\n  active run, flush session state to disk and release the agent. Never offload in\\n  the middle of a tool call or agent turn.\\n- Reconnect: a client may reconnect to the same session and ask for events after\\n  its last acknowledged sequence.\\n\\n## Scoped Tool Requirements\\n\\nThe Sheaf Chat Pi extension must provide scoped file and search tools for the\\nsession `rootDirectory`. It must not expose Bash, shell execution, or any general\\ncommand-execution tool.\\n\\nRequired tools:\\n\\n- `read`: same input/output shape and argument names as Pi's built-in `read`\\n  tool, but restricted to UTF-8 text files under the root and returning\\n  line-numbered excerpts with paths relativized to the root.\\n- `write`: same input/output shape and argument names as Pi's built-in `write`\\n  tool, but restricted to creating or overwriting files under the root and\\n  reporting only root-relative paths.\\n- `edit`: same input/output shape and argument names as Pi's built-in `edit`\\n  tool, including exact text replacement semantics, but restricted to files under\\n  the root and reporting only root-relative paths.\\n- `list`: list directory entries under the root with file type, size, and\\n  modified time.\\n- `tree`: return a bounded directory tree with ignore rules for dependency,\\n  build, VCS, cache, and large generated directories.\\n- `find_files`: ripgrep/fd-like file discovery by glob, extension, path segment,\\n  include/exclude globs, max depth, and limit.\\n- `search_text`: ripgrep-like full-text search with literal or regex modes,\\n  case sensitivity, include/exclude globs, context lines, multiline-safe output,\\n  binary-file skipping, and match limits.\\n- `file_info`: stat a relative path and report canonical in-root metadata.\\n\\nTool rules:\\n\\n- `read`, `write`, and `edit` must preserve Pi's normal tool schema so existing\\n  Pi prompting and model behavior remain compatible. Only path interpretation,\\n  validation, and result path rendering change.\\n- Tool path arguments use paths relative to the root directory.\\n- Absolute path input is rejected unless converted to a path under the root and\\n  returned/displayed as relative.\\n- Normalize, resolve symlinks where relevant, and verify the final target remains\\n  inside the canonical root before every filesystem operation.\\n- Search tools must provide enough capability to replace normal shell `rg`,\\n  `find`, `ls`, and lightweight code-navigation usage without granting arbitrary\\n  process execution.\\n- Tool results must redact or relativize absolute host paths under the root.\\n- Tool results must not reveal parent directories or files outside the root.\\n- Attempts to escape the root should emit a visible AGUI activity/control event\\n  and be logged for audit.\\n\\n## Providers And Models\\n\\nInitial providers:\\n\\n1. OpenAI subscription/OAuth, with OAuth data stored under `data/sheaf-chat/`.\\n2. Local inference, using `sheaf_chat.local_inference_url` from config and\\n   `sheaf_chat.local_api_key` from `config/api_keys.json`.\\n\\nThe model list exposed to browsers must merge:\\n\\n- GPT/OpenAI models available through the configured OpenAI subscription; and\\n- models reported by or configured for the local inference endpoint.\\n\\nThe server should expose model metadata indicating provider, model ID, display\\nname, context capability if known, and whether the model is currently available.\\n\\n## REST API\\n\\nAll JSON responses should include stable machine-readable errors:\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"error\\\": { \\\"code\\\": \\\"not_found\\\", \\\"message\\\": \\\"...\\\" } }\\n```\\n\\nRequired endpoints:\\n\\n- `GET /api/health` — service health and version.\\n- `GET /api/piles` — list piles with session counts and latest update time.\\n- `POST /api/piles` — create a pile. Body: `{ \\\"pile\\\": \\\"name\\\" }`.\\n- `GET /api/piles/:pile/sessions` — list session manifests in a pile, newest\\n  first, excluding heavy message history.\\n- `GET /api/piles/:pile/sessions/:sessionId` — return one manifest.\\n- `POST /api/piles/:pile/sessions` — create a new blank session shell. Body\\n  includes `{ \\\"rootDirectory\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"model\\\": { \\\"provider\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"...\\\" } }`.\\n  Response includes `sessionId`, provisional session metadata, and WebSocket URL,\\n  but not a persisted manifest. The manifest is written only after the first\\n  assistant message completes. The first user message may be sent over the\\n  WebSocket rather than this REST call.\\n- `GET /api/piles/:pile/sessions/:sessionId/history?before=<cursor>&limit=<n>` —\\n  optional REST fallback for paged history if WebSocket history is not available.\\n- `GET /api/models` — list available models.\\n\\nThe browser should normally use WebSocket history requests, but the REST history\\nfallback is useful for testing and recovery.\\n\\n## WebSocket Protocol\\n\\n### URL And Connection\\n\\nUse one WebSocket route for both new and resumed sessions:\\n\\n```text\\n/ws/chat?p=<pile>&session=<sessionId>&client=<clientId>&after=<sequence>\\n```\\n\\nFor a newly-created blank session, the client first calls\\n`POST /api/piles/:pile/sessions`, then opens this WebSocket and sends the first\\n`client.user_message`.\\n\\nQuery parameters:\\n\\n- `p` / `pile` (required): pile name.\\n- `session` (required): session ID.\\n- `client` (optional): stable browser client ID for reconnect diagnostics.\\n- `after` (optional): last server sequence the client has processed. If present,\\n  server sends all available envelopes after that sequence before live mode.\\n\\nAll WebSocket frames are UTF-8 JSON objects. Binary frames are not required for\\nquest zero.\\n\\n### Envelope\\n\\nEvery server-to-client and client-to-server frame uses this envelope:\\n\\n```ts\\ntype ChatEnvelope = {\\n  v: 1;\\n  kind: string;\\n  id: string;              // unique frame id generated by sender\\n  pile: string;\\n  sessionId: string;\\n  clientId?: string;\\n  sequence?: number;       // server-assigned monotonically increasing sequence\\n  timestamp: string;       // ISO-8601\\n  payload?: unknown;\\n};\\n```\\n\\nServer-assigned `sequence` values are strictly increasing per session and are the\\nbasis for replay, acknowledgements, and lazy loading. Client frames do not set\\n`sequence`.\\n\\n### Server-To-Client Kinds\\n\\n#### `server.hello`\\n\\nFirst frame after a successful connection.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"server.hello\\\",\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"connectionId\\\": \\\"...\\\",\\n    \\\"manifest\\\": null,\\n    \\\"provisionalSession\\\": {\\n      \\\"rootDirectory\\\": \\\"projects/example-app\\\",\\n      \\\"model\\\": { \\\"provider\\\": \\\"openai\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"gpt-5-codex\\\" }\\n    },\\n    \\\"latestSequence\\\": 123,\\n    \\\"historyWindow\\\": { \\\"oldestSequence\\\": 80, \\\"newestSequence\\\": 123 },\\n    \\\"models\\\": [],\\n    \\\"activeModel\\\": { \\\"provider\\\": \\\"openai\\\", \\\"id\\\": \\\"gpt-5-codex\\\" }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n#### `history.page`\\n\\nA page of historical AGUI events or snapshot messages. Sent in response to\\n`client.history_request` and optionally during connection bootstrap.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"history.page\\\",\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"requestId\\\": \\\"client-frame-id\\\",\\n    \\\"direction\\\": \\\"before\\\",\\n    \\\"events\\\": [ { \\\"type\\\": \\\"TEXT_MESSAGE_START\\\" } ],\\n    \\\"messages\\\": [ { \\\"id\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"role\\\": \\\"user\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"...\\\" } ],\\n    \\\"oldestSequence\\\": 1,\\n    \\\"newestSequence\\\": 50,\\n    \\\"hasMoreBefore\\\": false,\\n    \\\"hasMoreAfter\\\": true\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThe server may send either AGUI events or AGUI-compatible message snapshots. If\\nsnapshots are sent, they must match message shapes accepted by\\n`projects/web/src/agui-chat.js`.\\n\\n#### `agui.event`\\n\\nOne AGUI event mapped from Pi output or generated by Sheaf Chat.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"agui.event\\\",\\n  \\\"sequence\\\": 124,\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"type\\\": \\\"TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT\\\",\\n    \\\"messageId\\\": \\\"assistant-1\\\",\\n    \\\"delta\\\": \\\"Hello\\\"\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n`payload` must validate against `structure/schemas/ag_ui_events.schema.json` when\\npossible. Preserve raw Pi events in `rawEvent` for debugging unless they contain\\nsecrets or host-only paths.\\n\\n#### `chat.user_message`\\n\\nBroadcast copy of an accepted user message. The originating client receives this\\ntoo, so all clients render identical user turns.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"chat.user_message\\\",\\n  \\\"sequence\\\": 125,\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"messageId\\\": \\\"user-...\\\",\\n    \\\"text\\\": \\\"Please inspect src/app.ts\\\",\\n    \\\"attachments\\\": [],\\n    \\\"steer\\\": true\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThe server should also emit equivalent AGUI text message events so generic AGUI\\nreducers can display the message.\\n\\n#### `session.updated`\\n\\nManifest or session metadata changed, such as initial manifest creation after the\\nfirst assistant message, generated chat name, root display, message count, or\\nactive model.\\n\\n#### `model.changed`\\n\\nThe active model changed for future turns or, if Pi supports it, for the current\\nrun.\\n\\n#### `agent.status`\\n\\nLifecycle/status update. Payload examples: `{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"starting\\\" }`,\\n`{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"active\\\" }`, `{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"offloading\\\" }`,\\n`{ \\\"state\\\": \\\"resumed\\\" }`.\\n\\n#### `server.caught_up`\\n\\nThe server has finished replaying requested backlog and subsequent frames are\\nlive. This mirrors the existing Quest Runner dashboard behavior.\\n\\n#### `server.error`\\n\\nRecoverable or fatal error.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"server.error\\\",\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"code\\\": \\\"root_escape_denied\\\",\\n    \\\"message\\\": \\\"Path is outside the session root\\\",\\n    \\\"fatal\\\": false,\\n    \\\"requestId\\\": \\\"...\\\"\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n#### `server.pong`\\n\\nResponse to `client.ping`.\\n\\n### Client-To-Server Kinds\\n\\n#### `client.hello`\\n\\nOptional client capabilities after socket open.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.hello\\\",\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"supportsSnapshots\\\": true,\\n    \\\"supportsLazyHistory\\\": true,\\n    \\\"lastSeenSequence\\\": 123\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n#### `client.user_message`\\n\\nSubmit a user message.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.user_message\\\",\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"messageId\\\": \\\"client-generated-id\\\",\\n    \\\"text\\\": \\\"Continue, but use the local model.\\\",\\n    \\\"attachments\\\": [],\\n    \\\"steer\\\": true\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nRules:\\n\\n- The server validates, persists, sequences, and broadcasts the message before or\\n  while delivering it to the agent.\\n- If an agent turn is already running, the new message must steer the ongoing\\n  conversation if Pi supports steering/queueing. If Pi cannot steer mid-turn, the\\n  message must be queued as the next user input and all clients must still see it\\n  immediately.\\n- The server must de-duplicate by `messageId` for reconnect/retry safety.\\n\\n#### `client.history_request`\\n\\nRequest older or newer events/messages.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.history_request\\\",\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"before\\\": 80,\\n    \\\"after\\\": null,\\n    \\\"limit\\\": 50,\\n    \\\"prefer\\\": \\\"snapshots\\\"\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nSupported modes:\\n\\n- `{ \\\"before\\\": sequence }`: page older history for scroll-up loading.\\n- `{ \\\"after\\\": sequence }`: replay missed events after reconnect.\\n- no cursor: return latest page large enough to populate the screen.\\n\\nThe server responds with `history.page` and must not block live `agui.event`\\nbroadcasts while reading history.\\n\\n#### `client.model_select`\\n\\nSwitch model.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.model_select\\\",\\n  \\\"payload\\\": {\\n    \\\"provider\\\": \\\"local\\\",\\n    \\\"id\\\": \\\"qwen3-coder\\\",\\n    \\\"applyTo\\\": \\\"next_turn\\\"\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nIf AGUI later standardizes model selection, this control message may be mapped to\\nthat standard, but the Sheaf Chat protocol must support it now. The server\\nvalidates availability, updates the manifest, broadcasts `model.changed`, and\\napplies the change to Pi according to SDK capabilities.\\n\\n#### `client.ack`\\n\\nAcknowledge processed server sequence.\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"kind\\\": \\\"client.ack\\\", \\\"payload\\\": { \\\"sequence\\\": 125 } }\\n```\\n\\nAcks are used for diagnostics and reconnect hints. They are not required for\\nexactly-once delivery.\\n\\n#### `client.cancel` / `client.stop_generating`\\n\\nRequest cancellation of the current agent turn if supported. The server\\nbroadcasts status and emits AGUI lifecycle close/error events as needed.\\n\\n#### `client.ping`\\n\\nKeepalive. Server responds with `server.pong`.\\n\\n### Ordering And Synchronization\\n\\n- The server assigns sequence numbers after accepting an event for a session.\\n- All attached clients receive frames in sequence order for that session.\\n- User messages are persisted and broadcast even if the agent later fails.\\n- Agent output events are broadcast to all current clients and appended to the\\n  session log/history index.\\n- On reconnect, the client supplies `after=<lastSequence>` or sends\\n  `client.history_request` with `after`. The server replays missed frames, sends\\n  `server.caught_up`, then continues live.\\n- When multiple clients send user messages concurrently, the server serializes\\n  them by acceptance time and sequence number. That sequence is the conversation\\n  order.\\n\\n### AGUI Mapping Requirements\\n\\nThe server may either:\\n\\n1. reuse the existing Python mapping logic through a subprocess/module boundary;\\n   or\\n2. implement an equivalent TypeScript mapper for Pi JSON events.\\n\\nA TypeScript mapper is preferred for a Node-only backend if it can be tested\\nagainst the existing AGUI schema. Required mapped surfaces include:\\n\\n- user text messages;\\n- assistant text stream start/content/end;\\n- reasoning/thinking deltas where Pi exposes them;\\n- tool call start/arguments/result/end;\\n- run/turn start, finish, cancellation, and errors;\\n- custom Sheaf Chat activity events for path enforcement, model changes, and\\n  lifecycle status.\\n\\nUnrecognized Pi events must not be dropped. test("WebSocket rejects invalid pile and session query parameters", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const invalidPile = await WaitForOpenOrReject(
      `${handle.wsBaseUrl}/ws/chat?p=../evil&session=abc123`,
    );

    {
      assert.equal(invalidPile.status, 400);
    }

      `${handle.wsBaseUrl}/ws/chat?p=default`,

  });
});

test("new session first user message is broadcast with AGUI events", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const url = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId);

    await WithWebSocket(url, async (socket) =>
    {
      SendClientFrame(
        socket,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            messageId: "user-msg-1",
            text: "Hello agent",
            attachments: [],
            steer: true,
          },
          "frame-user-1",
        ),
      );

      const userBroadcast = await WaitForEnvelope(
        socket,
        (envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message",
      );
      const aguiStart = await WaitForEnvelope(
        socket,
        (envelope) =>
          envelope.kind === "agui.event" &&
          (envelope.payload as { type?: string }).type === "TEXT_MESSAGE_START",
      );

      assert.ok(userBroadcast.sequence !== undefined);
      assert.equal((userBroadcast.payload as { messageId: string }).messageId, "user-msg-1");
      assert.equal((userBroadcast.payload as { text: string }).text, "Hello agent");
      assert.ok(aguiStart.sequence !== undefined);
      assert.ok(aguiStart.sequence! > userBroadcast.sequence!);

      const fake = [...handle.fakeSessions.values()][0];
      assert.ok(fake);
      await WaitForCondition(() => fake.promptCalls.length === 1);
      assert.equal(fake.promptCalls[0]?.text, "Hello agent");
    });
  });
});

test("two clients on the same session receive identical broadcasts", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const urlA = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-a" });
    const urlB = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-b" });

    const connectedA = await ConnectWebSocket(urlA);
    const connectedB = await ConnectWebSocket(urlB);
    const socketA = connectedA.socket;
    const socketB = connectedB.socket;

    try
    {
      await DrainConnection(socketA);
      await DrainConnection(socketB);

      const collectedA: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectedB: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectorA = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedA.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      const collectorB = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedB.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      socketA.on("message", collectorA);
      socketB.on("message", collectorB);

      SendClientFrame(
        socketA,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            messageId: "shared-msg-1",
            text: "visible to both",
          },
        ),
      );

      await WaitForCondition(
        () =>
          collectedA.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message") &&
          collectedB.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message"),
      );

      socketA.off("message", collectorA);
      socketB.off("message", collectorB);

      const broadcastA = collectedA.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");
      const broadcastB = collectedB.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");

      assert.ok(broadcastA);
      assert.ok(broadcastB);
      assert.equal(broadcastA.sequence, broadcastB.sequence);
      assert.deepEqual(broadcastA.payload, broadcastB.payload);
    }
    finally
    {
      socketA.close();
      socketB.close();
    }
  });
});

test("duplicate client.user_message by messageId does not create duplicate broadcasts", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const url = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId);

    await WithWebSocket(url, async (socket) =>
    {
      const frame = CreateClientEnvelope(
        "client.user_message",
        session.pile,
        session.sessionId,
        {
          messageId: "retry-msg",
          text: "only once",
        },
      );

      SendClientFrame(socket, frame);
      await WaitForEnvelope(socket, (envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");
      SendClientFrame(socket, frame);

      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 100));

      const received: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const listener = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        received.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      socket.on("message", listener);
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
      socket.off("message", listener);

      const userMessages = received.filter((entry) => entry.kind === "chat.user_message");
      assert.equal(userMessages.length, 0);

      const fake = [...handle.fakeSessions.values()][0];
      assert.equal(fake?.promptCalls.length, 1);
    });
  });
});

test("client.history_request returns history.page for before and after cursors", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const storagePaths = CreateStoragePaths(handle.config.repoRoot);

    for (let index = 1; index <= 3; index += 1)
    {
      await AppendEnvelope(storagePaths, session.pile, session.sessionId, {
        kind: "chat.user_message",
        pile: session.pile,
        sessionId: session.sessionId,
        payload: {
          messageId: `msg-${index}`,
          text: `message ${index}`,
        },
      });
    }

    const url = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId);

    await WithWebSocket(url, async (socket) =>
    {
      SendClientFrame(
        socket,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.history_request",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            before: 3,
            limit: 10,
            prefer: "snapshots",
          },
          "history-before",
        ),
      );

      const beforePage = await WaitForEnvelope(
        socket,
        (envelope) => envelope.kind === "history.page",
      );
      const beforePayload = beforePage.payload as {
        requestId: string;
        direction: string;
        messages: unknown[];
        hasMoreBefore: boolean;
      };

      assert.equal(beforePayload.requestId, "history-before");
      assert.equal(beforePayload.direction, "before");
      assert.ok(beforePayload.messages.length >= 1);

      SendClientFrame(
        socket,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.history_request",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            after: 1,
            limit: 10,
            prefer: "events",
          },
          "history-after",
        ),
      );

      const afterPage = await WaitForEnvelope(
        socket,
        (envelope) =>
          envelope.kind === "history.page" &&
          (envelope.payload as { requestId?: string }).requestId === "history-after",
      );
      const afterPayload = afterPage.payload as {
        direction: string;
        events: unknown[];
        hasMoreAfter: boolean;
      };

      assert.equal(afterPayload.direction, "after");
      assert.ok(afterPayload.events.length >= 1);
    });
  });
});

test("two clients on the same session receive identical broadcasts", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const urlA = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-a" });
    const urlB = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-b" });

    const connectedA = await ConnectWebSocket(urlA);
    const connectedB = await ConnectWebSocket(urlB);
    const socketA = connectedA.socket;
    const socketB = connectedB.socket;

    try
    {
      await DrainConnection(socketA);
      await DrainConnection(socketB);

      const collectedA: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectedB: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectorA = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedA.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      const collectorB = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedB.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      socketA.on("message", collectorA);
      socketB.on("message", collectorB);

      SendClientFrame(
        socketA,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            messageId: "shared-msg-1",
            text: "visible to both",
          },
        ),
      );

      await WaitForCondition(
        () =>
          collectedA.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message") &&
          collectedB.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message"),
      );

      socketA.off("message", collectorA);
      socketB.off("message", collectorB);

      const broadcastA = collectedA.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");
      const broadcastB = collectedB.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");

      assert.ok(broadcastA);
      assert.ok(broadcastB);
      assert.equal(broadcastA.sequence, broadcastB.sequence);
      assert.deepEqual(broadcastA.payload, broadcastB.payload);
    }
    finally
    {
      socketA.close();
      socketB.close();
    }
  });
});

test("WebSocket connection sends server.hello then server.caught_up", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const url = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "browser-1" });

      assert.equal(hello?.pile, session.pile);

      assert.equal(hello?.clientId, "browser-1");

      const payload = hello?.payload as {
        connectionId: string;
        manifest: unknown;
        provisionalSession: { rootDirectory: string; model: { provider: string; id: string } };
        latestSequence: number;
        historyWindow: { oldestSequence: number | null; newestSequence: number | null };
        models: unknown[];
        activeModel: { provider: string; id: string };
      };

      assert.match(payload.connectionId, /^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
      assert.equal(payload.manifest, null);
      assert.ok(payload.provisionalSession);
      assert.ok(Array.isArray(payload.models));
      assert.ok(payload.activeModel.provider.length > 0);
      assert.equal(bootstrap[bootstrap.length - 1]?.kind, "server.caught_up");
    });
  });
});

test("two clients on the same session receive identical broadcasts", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const urlA = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-a" });
    const urlB = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-b" });

    const connectedA = await ConnectWebSocket(urlA);
    const connectedB = await ConnectWebSocket(urlB);
    const socketA = connectedA.socket;
    const socketB = connectedB.socket;

    try
    {
      await DrainConnection(socketA);
      await DrainConnection(socketB);

      const collectedA: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectedB: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectorA = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedA.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      const collectorB = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedB.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      socketA.on("message", collectorA);
      socketB.on("message", collectorB);

      SendClientFrame(
        socketA,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            messageId: "shared-msg-1",
            text: "visible to both",
          },
        ),
      );

      await WaitForCondition(
        () =>
          collectedA.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message") &&
          collectedB.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message"),
      );

      socketA.off("message", collectorA);
      socketB.off("message", collectorB);

      const broadcastA = collectedA.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");
      const broadcastB = collectedB.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");

      assert.ok(broadcastA);
      assert.ok(broadcastB);
      assert.equal(broadcastA.sequence, broadcastB.sequence);
      assert.deepEqual(broadcastA.payload, broadcastB.payload);
    }
    finally
    {
      socketA.close();
      socketB.close();
    }
  });
});

test("two clients on the same session receive identical broadcasts", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const urlA = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-a" });
    const urlB = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-b" });

    const connectedA = await ConnectWebSocket(urlA);
    const connectedB = await ConnectWebSocket(urlB);
    const socketA = connectedA.socket;
    const socketB = connectedB.socket;

    try
    {
      await DrainConnection(socketA);
      await DrainConnection(socketB);

      const collectedA: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectedB: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectorA = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedA.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      const collectorB = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedB.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      socketA.on("message", collectorA);
      socketB.on("message", collectorB);

      SendClientFrame(
        socketA,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            messageId: "shared-msg-1",
            text: "visible to both",
          },
        ),
      );

      await WaitForCondition(
        () =>
          collectedA.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message") &&
          collectedB.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message"),
      );

      socketA.off("message", collectorA);
      socketB.off("message", collectorB);

      const broadcastA = collectedA.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");
      const broadcastB = collectedB.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");

      assert.ok(broadcastA);
      assert.ok(broadcastB);
      assert.equal(broadcastA.sequence, broadcastB.sequence);
      assert.deepEqual(broadcastA.payload, broadcastB.payload);
    }
    finally
    {
      socketA.close();
      socketB.close();
    }
  });
});

  {

            limit: 10,
            prefer: "snapshots",

          "history-before",

        (envelope) => envelope.kind === "history.page",

        direction: string;
        messages: unknown[];
        hasMoreBefore: boolean;
      };

        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.history_request",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            after: 1,
            limit: 10,
            prefer: "events",
          },
          "history-after",
        ),
      );

        socket,

    });
  });

test("WebSocket connection sends server.hello then server.caught_up", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const url = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "browser-1" });

    await WithWebSocket(url, async (_socket, bootstrap) =>
    {
      const hello = bootstrap.find((entry) => entry.kind === "server.hello");

      assert.ok(hello);
      assert.equal(hello?.pile, session.pile);
      assert.equal(hello?.sessionId, session.sessionId);
      assert.equal(hello?.clientId, "browser-1");

      const payload = hello?.payload as {
        connectionId: string;
        manifest: unknown;
        provisionalSession: { rootDirectory: string; model: { provider: string; id: string } };
        latestSequence: number;
        historyWindow: { oldestSequence: number | null; newestSequence: number | null };
        models: unknown[];
        activeModel: { provider: string; id: string };
      };

      assert.match(payload.connectionId, /^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
      assert.equal(payload.manifest, null);
      assert.ok(payload.provisionalSession);
      assert.ok(Array.isArray(payload.models));
      assert.ok(payload.activeModel.provider.length > 0);
      assert.equal(bootstrap[bootstrap.length - 1]?.kind, "server.caught_up");
    });
  });
});

test("two clients on the same session receive identical broadcasts", async () =>
{

  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);

    const urlB = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId, { clientId: "client-b" });

    const connectedA = await ConnectWebSocket(urlA);
    const connectedB = await ConnectWebSocket(urlB);
    const socketA = connectedA.socket;
    const socketB = connectedB.socket;

    try
    {
      await DrainConnection(socketA);
      await DrainConnection(socketB);

      const collectedA: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectedB: ChatEnvelope[] = [];
      const collectorA = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedA.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      const collectorB = (data: Buffer) =>
      {
        collectedB.push(JSON.parse(data.toString()) as ChatEnvelope);
      };
      socketA.on("message", collectorA);
      socketB.on("message", collectorB);

      SendClientFrame(
        socketA,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          {
            messageId: "shared-msg-1",
            text: "visible to both",
          },
        ),
      );

      await WaitForCondition(
        () =>
          collectedA.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message") &&
          collectedB.some((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message"),
      );

      socketA.off("message", collectorA);
      socketB.off("message", collectorB);

      const broadcastA = collectedA.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");
      const broadcastB = collectedB.find((envelope) => envelope.kind === "chat.user_message");

      assert.ok(broadcastA);
      assert.ok(broadcastB);
      assert.equal(broadcastA.sequence, broadcastB.sequence);
      assert.deepEqual(broadcastA.payload, broadcastB.payload);
    }
    finally
    {
      socketA.close();
      socketB.close();
    }
  });
});

test("concurrent user messages are sequenced monotonically", async () =>
{
  await WithWebSocketTestServer(async (handle) =>
  {
    const session = await CreateBlankSessionViaApi(handle);
    const url = BuildWsUrl(handle, session.pile, session.sessionId);

    await WithWebSocket(url, async (socket) =>
    {
      SendClientFrame(
        socket,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          { messageId: "concurrent-a", text: "A" },
        ),
      );
      SendClientFrame(
        socket,
        CreateClientEnvelope(
          "client.user_message",
          session.pile,
          session.sessionId,
          { messageId: "concurrent-b", text: "B" },
        ),
      );

      const first = await WaitForEnvelope(
        socket,
        (envelope) =>
          envelope.kind === "chat.user_message" &&
          (envelope.payload as { messageId?: string }).messageId === "concurrent-a",
      );
      const second = await WaitForEnvelope(
        socket,
        (envelope) =>
          envelope.kind === "chat.user_message" &&
          (envelope.payload as { messageId?: string }).messageId === "concurrent-b",
      );

      assert.ok(first.sequence !== undefined);
      assert.ok(second.sequence !== undefined);
      assert.ok(second.sequence! > first.sequence!);
    });
  });
});

title: history.page events mode duplicates user messages (chat.user_message re-mapped on top of stored agui.event)
owner_role: polisher_reviewer

body:
  ## Problem

  `ExtractAguiEvents` in `src/protocol/sessionBroadcaster.ts` double-counts user
  messages when building `history.page` payloads, producing duplicate user turns
  in `prefer: "events"` mode.

  For every history envelope it does:
  - if `kind === "agui.event"`: push the stored AGUI payload, and
  - if `kind === "chat.user_message"`: push `mapUserMessageToAgui(...)` of the
    same message.

  But `ProcessUserMessage` persists BOTH a `chat.user_message` envelope AND the
  mapped `agui.event` envelopes (TEXT_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END) for that same
  user message. So for a session produced by the live flow, the history log
  contains both representations, and `ExtractAguiEvents` emits the user
  message's text events twice.

  In `HandleHistoryRequest`, when `prefer === "events"` the raw (duplicated)
  event list is returned directly in `payload.events`. (In the default
  `snapshots` mode the duplication is masked because `eventsToSnapshots` dedups
  by `messageId`.)

  ## Why it is a problem

  A client requesting history in events mode (`prefer: "events"`, a supported
  mode) renders each user turn twice on scroll-up / reconnect-after paging. The
  existing test "client.history_request returns history.page for before and after
  cursors" does not catch this because its history is hand-seeded with
  `chat.user_message` entries only (no accompanying `agui.event` entries), so the
  double-mapping path is never exercised against a realistic live-produced log.

  ## What must be true to close

  - For a session whose log was produced by the normal user-message flow (both
    `chat.user_message` and its mapped `agui.event` entries present), a
    `history_request` with `prefer: "events"` returns each user message's text
    events exactly once (no duplication).
  - The fix chooses a single source of truth for user-message events in history
    extraction (use the stored `agui.event` entries, or re-map from
    `chat.user_message`, but not both).
  - A test seeds a log containing both `chat.user_message` and its
    `agui.event` entries and asserts the events-mode page has no duplicated user
    turn.

body:
  ## Problem

  A newly-connected client is added to the broadcast set **before** `server.hello`,
  the `after` replay, and `server.caught_up` are sent, so live frames can be
  delivered out of the spec-mandated order.

  In `AttachChatWebSocketConnection` (`src/server/websocket.ts`):

  ```
  const client = broadcaster.RegisterClient(socket, params.clientId); // joins m_clients now
  await SendHello(client, ...);            // awaits attachSession + HistoryWindow (file I/O)
  await SendReplayAndCaughtUp(client, ...) // awaits replay then sends caught_up
  ```

  `RegisterClient` inserts the socket into `m_clients`, and
  `SessionBroadcaster.Broadcast` fans out to every entry in `m_clients`. Because
  `SendHello` / `SendReplayAndCaughtUp` contain multiple `await`s, any lifecycle
  event that fires during that window (`agent.status`, `agui.event`,
  `model.changed`, `session.updated`, `server.error`) is broadcast to the new
  socket before `server.hello` and/or interleaved with replay before
  `server.caught_up`.

  This is not just a hot-attach edge case: for a brand-new session, `SendHello`
  calls `agentManager.attachSession`, which starts the runtime and synchronously
  emits `Starting`/`Active` status transitions. The broadcaster's status handler
  persists+broadcasts `agent.status` frames during `attachSession`, so the very
  first frames a fresh client receives can be `agent.status` before
  `server.hello`.

  ## Why it is a problem

  The spec is explicit:
  - `server.hello` is "the first frame after a successful connection."
  - `server.caught_up` means "the server has finished replaying requested backlog
    and subsequent frames are live."

  Delivering live `agent.status`/`agui.event` frames before `server.hello`, or
  interleaving them into the replay window before `server.caught_up`, breaks the
  client bootstrap contract (connectionId/models/historyWindow must arrive first;
  backlog must be bounded by caught_up). It can also double-deliver an envelope
  that is both broadcast live and included in the `after` replay read.

  The existing test "WebSocket connection sends server.hello then
  server.caught_up" does NOT catch this: it locates hello with
  `bootstrap.find(...)` rather than asserting it is the first frame, so a status
  frame arriving before hello still passes.

  ## What must be true to close

  - A connection must not receive any broadcast frame until after `server.hello`
    and `server.caught_up` have been sent to it (e.g. register into the broadcast
    set only after caught_up, or buffer/queue outbound frames during bootstrap and
    flush them after caught_up).
  - `server.hello` is guaranteed to be the first frame; no live frame precedes it
    and no live frame is interleaved into the replay window before
    `server.caught_up`.
  - A test asserts ordering explicitly: hello is the first frame, and for a
    session with active lifecycle emissions during attach, no `agent.status` /
    `agui.event` frame is observed before `server.hello` or between the start of
    replay and `server.caught_up`.

body:
  ## Problem

  WebSocket connection liveness (which drives idle offload of the agent) is
  tracked by the optional `client` query parameter, not by the actual socket
  connection.

  Flow:
  - `AttachChatWebSocketConnection` -> `SendHello` -> `agentManager.attachSession(pile, sessionId, clientId)`
    -> `SessionRuntime.AttachClient(clientId)`.
  - On socket close -> `agentManager.markClientDetached(key, clientId)` ->
    `SessionRuntime.DetachClient(clientId)`.

  `SessionRuntime.AttachClient`/`DetachClient` only mutate `m_record.clients`
  when `clientId !== undefined && clientId.length > 0`. The idle-offload
  scheduler (`ScheduleIdleOffload`, `CanOffload`) gates entirely on
  `m_record.clients.size === 0`.

  The slice spec marks `client` as optional:
  "client (optional): stable browser client ID for reconnect diagnostics."

  Consequences:
  1. A connection opened without a `client` param never increments
     `m_record.clients`, so the runtime believes zero clients are attached. After
     `agent_end` (or immediately on the idle path) `ScheduleIdleOffload` runs and
     the agent is torn down (pi session disposed, state -> Cold) while the
     WebSocket is still open and live.
  2. Two connections sharing the same `client` id are stored once in the Set;
     closing one removes the id even though the other is still connected,
     triggering premature offload.

  ## Why it is a problem

  The agent can be offloaded out from under an active, connected client whenever
  the optional `client` param is absent or shared. The spec's intent is that idle
  offload happens when there are no connected WebSockets, not no client ids.
  While a subsequent `client.user_message` will re-attach via cold resume, the
  disposal causes unnecessary churn and loss of in-flight streaming state for a
  client that never disconnected.

  ## What must be true to close

  - Idle-offload accounting reflects the number of live WebSocket connections for
    `(pile, sessionId)`, independent of whether/what `client` param was supplied
    (e.g. count connections by `connectionId`, or have the broadcaster's
    connection count drive offload).
  - A connection that omits `client` keeps the agent active for as long as the
    socket is open; offload only occurs after the last socket for the session
    closes (plus idle timeout).
  - A test covers attach/detach with no `client` param (and/or two connections
    sharing a `client` id) and asserts the agent is not offloaded while a socket
    remains connected.
